questions.extractedQuestion: Prove that the relation “friendship” is not an equivalence relation on the set of all people in Chennai.
steps: An equivalence relation must be reflexive, symmetric, and transitive.
Consider three people A, B, C in Chennai: A and B are friends, and B and C are friends, but A and C are not friends.
Then A R B and B R C hold, but A R C does not hold.
Thus friendship need not be transitive, so it is not an equivalence relation. This single counterexample is enough; we do not need to decide whether everyone is a friend of themselves.

questions.extractedQuestion: On the set of natural numbers let R be the relation defined by aRb if a + b ≤ 6. Write down the relation by listing all the pairs. Check whether it is (i) reflexive (ii) symmetric (iii) transitive (iv) equivalence
steps: Assume natural numbers are 1, 2, 3, ... . Since a+b≤6, both a and b must be at most 5.
List every ordered pair of positive integers whose sum is at most 6; there are 15 pairs.
Symmetric: whenever a+b≤6, b+a≤6, so reversing a pair stays in R.
Not transitive: (5,1) and (1,5) are in R, but (5,5) is not.
Therefore R is not an equivalence relation.

verification.method: exhaustive finite pair enumeration for a,b in 1..5
